items.title: Tom Albert Interview, 1962-05-07
items.q: Louie, Louie Nelson. Did you ever hear this name? Yeah, I heard him.

ctx.x: Was he a reader or head man or what?

No, he was head, yeah he's a head man. Yeah, all. Yeah. You know, just know them how they read music. But Poissy and his brother. Now, them fellas there used to be, now all, most of all Jack Carey, band always, break time. All by the people, so. Louie, Louie Nelson. Did you ever hear this name? Yeah, I heard him. Yeah? He wasn't reading then. No. Never did read, huh?
No, no. Never did read, huh? No, no, never did read. And there were, the fella playing the trombone, what do you call them again, from Al Jays.

items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...you remember Louie? Louie, Louie Nelson, eh? ... [INTERVIEWEE] That's an old band.

ctx.x: Johnny Gould. Johnny Gould. What'd he play? I don't know. Ford. Mitchell. Johnny Gould used to play violin. Violin. Mitchell used to play ghetto. Ford used to play bass. And when we used to go to the island, we used to, you remember Louie? Louie, Louie Nelson, eh? Oh, that's right.
